result.killer: No single killer was found. The free TLV Excel template and data dictionary, together with existing POS sales exports, cover most of the job. The duty is light: five product types, monthly totals, filed once a year.
result.reason: I found no dedicated app, POS feature or association tool (AACS) for the TLV record-keeping duty, so no product kills it. But the core job is small. Monthly totals for five product types (cigarette, cigar, little cigar, loose tobacco, bidi), purchased and sold, are filed once a year at renewal. TLV gives a free optional Excel template and a data dictionary, and accepts csv/xlsx/ods. A category-filtered POS export plus wholesaler invoices covers most of it. Vic market is about 3,300+ applications (Jan 2026 media release). I could not confirm NSW or Qld record-keeping duties beyond holding a licence (SA requires keeping supplier invoices for 2 years). Margins are thin, so willingness to pay is likely low. At best this is a feature for a POS vendor.

result.competitor: AUSTRAC publishes a free Jeweller Program Starter Kit. It is built for small jewellers with 15 or fewer staff that provide one designated service, which is exactly this candidate's buyer, and it covers the program-building job. easyAML sells a Tranche 2 platform that, by its own description, targets precious metals dealers and jewellers. It has a guided builder for an industry-specific AML/CTF program, identity and PEP/sanctions checks, and three pricing tiers. NameScan has a precious-metals industry page (namescan.io/industries/preciousmetals) offering screening and KYB. First AML and Arctic Intelligence sell general Tranche 2 tools. Persona and didit cover customer identity checks. Between the free state kit and easyAML, the core job is already done.
result.duty: The duty is real and in force under the Commonwealth AML/CTF Act as amended by the Tranche 2 reforms. Secondary sources agree on the details: Bartier Perry (law firm), Jeweller Magazine, easyAML and didit. I could not open AUSTRAC's own pages (HTTP 503 twice). Obligations started on 1 Jul 2026. Enrolment opened on 31 Mar 2026, and the enrolment deadline was 29 Jul 2026, not 31 Mar as the claim says. A dealer is captured only when it accepts or pays A$10,000 or more in physical cash or virtual assets, in one transaction or in linked ones. A captured dealer must enrol, hold a risk assessment and an AML/CTF program, verify customers and train staff. It must lodge a threshold transaction report within 10 business days and a suspicious matter report within 3 business days (24 hours if terrorism financing is suspected). An independent review is due every 3 years (vendor claim, not confirmed). Two opt-outs exist: a 'soft opt out' (refuse cash of A$10,000 or more) and a 'hard opt out' (take no cash or virtual assets for these sales). Neither requires enrolment, so many small jewellers can avoid the duty altogether. Penalties are civil penalties under the AML/CTF Act; I did not find the exact amounts. I did not check whether state second-hand dealer registers add a separate duty.
result.market: I found no register count or official estimate. AUSTRAC enrolment numbers for dealers were not found in this session. The buyers who actually carry the duty are only those who choose to accept cash of A$10,000 or more. That is a minority of an estimated few thousand jewellers and bullion dealers, a figure I did not confirm. Bullion and scrap-gold buyers are the most likely to remain captured.
result.reason: The duty is real and has applied since 1 Jul 2026. However, the claim's 31 Mar 2026 enrolment date is wrong: enrolment opened then and the deadline was 29 Jul 2026. A dealer only carries the duty if it chooses to take A$10,000 or more in cash or virtual assets, and the soft and hard opt-outs let most small jewellers avoid it completely. AUSTRAC's free starter kit targets this exact group (15 or fewer staff), and easyAML already sells a Tranche 2 platform that names precious metals dealers and jewellers. NameScan also has a precious-metals offering. That leaves a small, self-selecting group of captured dealers, mostly bullion and scrap-gold buyers, served by free and paid tools. A jeweller-specific niche is weak at best.

result.competitor: I found no Australian SaaS built for AS/NZS 3666 or NSW Form 3. Partial coverage comes from water-treatment contractors who already run the monthly testing and bundle the reporting. BrodexTrident has a client portal for certificates and test results, and Nalco Water (Ecolab) offers NATA lab reports with online customer access. UK tools that could be adapted include Joblogic, TEAMS Legionella and the Legionella Compliance App. General monitoring platforms include Optima Tower and Integra iTrack. Nobody offers a state portal for lodgement: NSW lodges with councils, and Victoria takes registrations by email (legionella@health.vic.gov.au). I did not check whether councils accept electronic lodgement in general.
result.duty: NSW: Public Health Act 2010 and Public Health Regulation 2022 (Part 2) set these duties. Register with council within 1 month of installation or change (Form 6). Test monthly for Legionella and HCC, with a monthly report (Approved Form 3). Notify council within 24 hours if Legionella is at least 1,000 cfu/mL or HCC at least 5,000,000 cfu/mL (Form 4). Renew the risk management plan every 5 years (Form 1). Have an annual independent audit (Form 2). Send certificates to council within 7 days. Display the tower ID within 30 days. The occupier stays liable even when a contractor fills in the forms. Vic: Public Health and Wellbeing Act 2008 requires per-tower registration with the Department of Health for 1, 2 or 3 years (2025-26 fee $126.10 for 1 year), notice of changes or decommissioning within 30 days, and an annual audit of the risk management plan. Failing to register, prepare a risk management plan or audit it is an offence. Penalty amounts were not checked. Tas councils also register cooling towers (Devonport form). Qld, WA and SA were not reached.
result.market: I found no statewide count. NSW registers sit with each council and have no central total. Victoria has a public register but publishes no total figure. One local indicator: 89 towers were tested in a few Sydney CBD blocks during the 2016 outbreak. The total is likely in the low thousands per state (an estimate, not verified), and mostly on commercial, hospital, hotel and retail buildings rather than small businesses.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. Under the NSW Public Health Regulation 2022, owners must register with council within 1 month, test monthly (Form 3), notify council within 24 hours of high results, renew the risk management plan every 5 years, have an annual independent audit, and send certificates to council within 7 days. Victoria requires per-tower registration for 1–3 years, an annual audit and 30-day change notices. I found no dedicated Australian software. However, the contractors who already test each month usually handle the work, and some offer client portals (BrodexTrident; Nalco/Ecolab online lab reports). Most towers sit on mid-to-large commercial buildings rather than small firms. The market is small and split across councils, and buyers would pay little extra.

result.competitor: I found no Australian software or register-and-reminder product for radiation compliance in dental or vet practices; my searches covered dental compliance software, vet compliance platforms and services from radiation experts. What exists is free: NSW EPA plan templates (dental and veterinary .docx), the EPA's Guideline 2, the Health Vic dental plan template, the ADA SA template, ADA NSW information sheets, and ADA Practice Plus (Vic) help with compliance. iComply and Dentistry Compliance do this kind of reminder tracking in the UK but not in Australia. VET.CT runs a free radiation safety hub. I did not check whether practice-management vendors (Exact, D4W, ezyVet) offer a radiation module, or whether radiation-expert firms send test reminders.
result.duty: NSW: Protection from Harmful Radiation Regulation 2025 (in force since 1 Dec 2025). Since 1 Sep 2026, holders of a radiation management licence must have a radiation management plan and comply with it. Copies must be available to users and staff, and the plan must follow the ARPANSA codes (dental RPS 10, veterinary RPS 17). The plan only goes to the EPA if the EPA asks for it. Per ADA NSW: dental premises need a radiation management licence, each X-ray unit needs its own RRM ID listed on the licence, and an accredited Consulting Radiation Expert must certify and test each unit at install, every 5 years, and after a tube-head replacement or a move; incidents must be reported. The NSW vet template requires a service log for each unit. SA (Radiation Protection and Control Act 2021): no licence is granted without an RMP the EPA has approved; the amended plan must be resubmitted after significant changes; new equipment needs registration and a compliance test within 60 days. Per ADA SA, cyclic 5-yearly testing and annual servicing stopped being required from 1 Feb 2026. Qld requires a radiation safety and protection plan; ACT requires a licence, source registration and a plan; Tasmania requires yearly licence renewal by 31 Aug and vet unit testing every 4 years. I did not confirm NSW penalty amounts or the licence term.
result.market: Not reached. I found no published NSW EPA count of radiation management licence holders. The EPA has a public licence search, but no dataset, so a count would need the EPA annual report or a formal information request. WA's Radiological Council publishes a list of vet licences (I did not count it). The buyers are likely a few thousand dental practices and vet clinics per state, but I have no source for that figure.
result.reason: The duty is real. The NSW EPA and the Protection from Harmful Radiation Regulation 2025 make a radiation management plan (RMP) a licence condition from 1 Sep 2026. Per ADA NSW, each X-ray unit needs an RRM ID, and an accredited radiation expert must test it at install, every 5 years and after a tube-head replacement or move. SA, ACT and Qld also require a plan. I found no Australian software that does this job, only free EPA, Health Vic and ADA templates. But the timing is poor. The 1 Sep 2026 deadline has passed, so writing the plan is now largely a one-off. What recurs is weak: yearly licence renewal, 5-yearly testing, and updating the plan after changes. SA dropped 5-yearly testing and annual servicing from Feb 2026. Buyers can fill in the templates for free, so willingness to pay looks low. I could not get a count of licence holders.

result.competitor: I found no dedicated Australian app or software for TLV record keeping or returns. Searches naming Idealpos, Retail Express, Lightspeed, Abacus and SwiftPOS returned nothing that links any of them to TLV reporting. A free state tool partly covers the core job: TLV publishes a data dictionary and an optional example data-collection template (Excel), and accepts csv/xlsx, so a spreadsheet or a filtered POS export can meet the duty. I did not check for association tools (AACS, Tobacconists Association): not_reached.
result.duty: Victoria: the Tobacco Act 1987 and Tobacco Regulations 2017. A licence has been required for each premises since 1 Feb 2026; it costs $1,175.20 to apply and $829.60 to renew each year (FY licence). Licensees keep wholesale purchase records (invoice, wholesaler licence number, ABN and similar) for at least 2 years. They record monthly totals of products purchased and sold by product type, in fixed units (cigarette packet of 20, cigar, little cigar packet of 20, 30g loose tobacco, bidi packet of 20), tagged with the licence number. These go to TLV electronically with the annual renewal; the 2026 reporting period is Feb-Dec 2026. Penalties for breaching licence conditions are up to $12,546 for a person and $62,730 for a business; for failing to display the licence, $209 or $1,046. NSW (from 1 Jul 2025): $1,100 per licence each year, licence displayed at point of sale, maximum penalty $220,000 for a corporation. Qld (from 1 Sep 2024): licence displayed. I did not find monthly record or return duties in NSW or Qld (not_reached).
result.market: I found no current licence count. TLV runs a public register at vic.gov.au/tobacco-register (updated weekly, last update 2 Oct 2026), but it shows no total and has no downloadable dataset. Qld had an estimated 8,000 tobacco retailers in a 2016 parliamentary submission (old). By inference, each eastern state probably has several thousand licensed premises, but this is unverified.
result.reason: The Victorian duty is real. Every licensee (retail and wholesale, one licence per premises) must keep purchase records for 2 years and record monthly counts of tobacco bought and sold by product type and fixed unit, under the Tobacco Regulations 2017. The data goes to TLV electronically (xlsx/xls/csv/ods only) at the annual renewal, with penalties up to $62,730 for a business. I found no dedicated software. But TLV publishes a free data dictionary and an optional Excel template, and the return is a simple yearly table that a spreadsheet or POS export can produce. So the pain is low, filing is once a year, and margins are thin, although many buyers (often multilingual) are reachable through wholesalers. I did not find NSW or Qld record-keeping duties of this kind.

result.competitor: The claim that there is "no standalone third-party multi-state tracker" is wrong. Oho validates WWCC or equivalent cards in ACT, NT, Qld (Blue Card, exemption and teacher cards), SA, Vic, Tas and WA. It re-checks every validated card each week and sends automated expiry reports. Gymnastics Australia and Basketball Victoria already use it. Oho cannot validate NSW cards because of NSW law; ACT cards are sighted in person and logged. Safe Ministry Check, built for churches, verifies WWCC numbers automatically with the relevant state authority and emails before expiry. ChurchSuite has a WWCC renewal workflow. Qld's free Organisation Portal sends expiry notices. Sports bodies build this into their member systems (Surfguard, PlaySafe/Oho).
result.duty: The duty is real and current, and it is ongoing. NSW organisations must register with the OCG employer portal, verify each WWC number, re-verify on renewal and keep their own records (date, outcome, expiry), because the portal keeps no history of past checks. In Qld, organisations must link card holders before work starts. Board and committee members need blue cards whatever their title. Expiry notices go to linked organisations at 10 weeks, 4 weeks, 2 weeks and 2 days. SA clubs must verify before work starts and at least every 5 years through an Organisation Portal. In Vic, organisations must make sure workers hold a valid Check. WA penalties go up to $60,000 plus possible imprisonment (per a SA/WA club resource sheet; not checked against the statute). I did not confirm the 20 Sept 2025 Qld committee-member start date. A law-firm page says new suspension powers began on that date.

result.reason: The duty is real, mandatory and ongoing. But the core job, automated multi-state verification with re-checks and expiry alerts, is already done. Oho covers every state except NSW with weekly re-checks and is used by national sports bodies. Safe Ministry Check covers churches. fit2work, CVCheck and Certn serve employers. Victoria and Qld offer free bulk tools or portals. NSW is the one gap, and it exists because the law blocks third-party validation, so a newcomer could not fill it either. Buyers are volunteer-run with little budget and are often served through their peak bodies' member systems. result.duty: Confirmed for NSW from nsw.gov.au (Strata Schemes Management Act 2015 as amended). Each item has its own date. From 1 Apr 2026, the standard form is required for a 10-year capital works fund plan when the plan is revised or replaced. Strata Hub also handles annual reporting, and two-lot schemes stop reporting from 1 Oct 2026. Committee training is a free government course. What's left is levy notices, AGM packs and records. Generic accounting tools plus StrataView (free version, listed for self-managed schemes) may cover that, but I didn't check StrataView's features. Buyers are unpaid volunteers with little willingness to pay, and rules differ by state. I found no count of self-managed schemes.

Duty is real: from 1 Jan 2027 all sheep and goats need an NLIS eID before leaving a property. Receiver must record P2P transfers on the NLIS database within 2 days (48 hours).
